This appeal is by the claimant filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.06.2023 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VII, Vijayapura in MVC No.207/2022 seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 31.10.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., on Karakamb-Bose road near Sugaon Bose, when the petitioner was sitting by the side of road with motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-13/CE-5280, at that time, a Tipper No.MH-13/AX-4604 came there being driven by its driver in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner and his motorcycle resulting in the accident.
Due to the said impact, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, after the accident, he was shifted to Dr.G.D. Patil Hospital,
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR Pandharpur and there he was taken to Aster Adhar Hospital,
Kolhapur, wherein he was treated as in-patient and inspite of spending huge amount, he has not fully recovered and suffered permanent physical impairment.
3. The petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy, aged about 19 years and was doing agriculture work and also milk and egg vending, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accident, he is unable continue his work.
Therefore, the claimant filed the petition under Section 166 of the Act before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
appeared and filed their separate written statement.
In their written statements they have denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR 5.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The petitioner, in order to prove the case, examined himself as PW-1 besides Abhijit Anil Pawar vs Shantaram Annappa Naik And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135531885/
3 examining the doctor as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely, Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.

sentences.text:
On behalf of respondents, no witness is examined but got marked copy of insurance policy as Ex.R.1.
6.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tipper, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.25,03,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR Tribunal, the present appeal is filed seeking enhancement of compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injury.
He has examined the doctor as P.W.2, who deposed that left lower limb of the claimant has been amputated above knee and has suffered disability of 80% to the whole body.
But, the Tribunal has assessed 70% disability to the whole body and the same is on the lower side.

b) He further contended that due to the accident, the petitioner has suffered 80%
disability and he was admitted to hospital as an in-patient for a period of 17 days.

During the treatment, he has suffered lot of pain and suffering and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and NC:
2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR other accidental expenses are on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation.
8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 - insurance company contend that at the time accident the claimant was aged about 19 years.
He has examined doctor as P.W.2, who assessed the disability at 80% to the whole body.

The Tribunal considering the medical records,
discharge summary and disability certificate has rightly come to the conclusion that the whole body disability of the claimant is 70%.
9.

Lastly, he has contended that considering the evidence of doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities,
other incidental injuries are just and reasonable.
Hence, she sought for dismissal of the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR 10.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and also the appeal papers.
11. It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injury in a road traffic accident occurred on 31.10.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tipper bearing Reg.No.MH-13/AX-4604.

sentences.text: is also not in dispute that due to the above accident, the claimant's left lower limb was amputated above the knee.
He examined the doctor as PW.2.
In his evidence, P.W.2 deposed that the claimant's left lower limb was amputated above the knee and assessed disability at 80%.
Even as per item No.17 of the Schedule appended to Employees Compensation Act, 1923, if the injury is amputation below hip, then disability has to be assessed at 80%.
Accordingly, considering the evidence of the doctor, medical records, disability certificate, we are of the opinion that whole body disability has to be assessed at 80%.

Insofar as the income of the claimant, the Tribunal has NC:
2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR rightly considered the income of the claimant at Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Since the claimant has suffered 80% disability, it affects his avocation and therefore in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of ERUDHAYA PRIYA VS STATE EXPRESS TRANSPORT CORPORATION reported in [2020 SCC ONLINE SC 601], the claimant is also entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: ERUDHAYA PRIYA VS STATE EXPRESS TRANSPORT CORPORATION reported in [2020 SCC ONLINE SC 601]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. At the time of accident, the claimant was aged about 19 years and the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of '18'.
In view of judgment of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi And Others [AIR 2017 SC 5157], 40% of income of the claimant has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi And Others [AIR 2017 SC 5157]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. Accordingly, loss of future earning has been re- assessed as under:
The 80% of income of Rs.15,000/- of the claimant comes to Rs.12,000/-.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injury.
He was in-patient for a period of 17 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during the treatment because of disability and has to suffer unhappiness during his life.

Considering the evidence of doctor and injury suffered by the claimant,
we are inclined to enhance the compensation towards 'pain and suffering' from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.75,000/-.
The compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head 'loss of amenities' is enhanced to Rs.60,000/-.
The claimant is also entitled for compensation towards loss of income during laid up period for a period of six months Rs.75,000/- (Rs.15,000/- x 5).
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads are just and reasonable.

15. On re-assessment and re-determination, the computation of compensation is as under:

In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.39,98,800/- as against - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6568-DB HC-KAR Rs.25,03,000/- awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

d) The Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit entire compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the Abhijit Anil Pawar vs Shantaram Annappa Naik And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135531885/
